observed_vs_expected: best_target_score was expected to rise as thicknesses deviated from quarter-wave values, but it declined from 0.95315 (R1) to 0.83504 (R3). Direction: lower. Magnitude: 0.11811 absolute drop across three rounds. valid_candidates expected to remain high and observed at 9, consistent. tightest_margin expected to stay above zero and observed at 0.93734, consistent. The hypothesis that simple deviations would balance the bands was refuted; instead, the score depressed immediately upon optimization, indicating the initial state was closer to the global optimum than the explored deviations.
deviation_mechanism: The optimizer's perturbations displaced layers past their coherent phase-matching points. The starting configuration naturally satisfied the dual-band balance, but broad step sizes moved key resonant layers (e.g., layer 6 shifting from 131.0 nm to ~90.4–94.7 nm in later candidates) out of their Fabry-Pérot resonance windows. This altered the optical path lengths required for constructive interference at 400 nm and 700 nm simultaneously, increasing cumulative phase error and degrading the composite score. Because tightest_margin remains positive at 0.93734, boundary constraints are not violated; the degradation is purely an optical interference effect caused by excessive thickness variation rather than physical infeasibility.
continue_rationale: Although the score fell rather than rose, the route exhibits no signs of physical collapse or algorithmic stall. valid_candidates holds steady at 9 and tightest_margin remains robust at 0.93734, confirming ample feasible design space. The absolute change from R2 to R3 is |-0.00408|, which exceeds the reference epsilon of 0.0001, proving the optimizer is still actively traversing parameter space. The current trajectory reflects an over-perturbed search wandering into suboptimal interference regimes; a more focused, locally anchored strategy can recover the performance lost to excessive thickness shifts.
insight_for_next: Reinitialize the optimizer around the Round 1 candidate geometry (thicknesses: [59.0, 95.0, 64.0, 91.0, 100.0, 131.0, 57.0, 98.0, 96.0, 91.0, 61.0, 90.0]) and tighten thickness exploration bounds to ±15 nm of these baseline values. insight_grounding: The R1 candidate set featuring layer 6 at 131.0 nm, layer 2 at 95.0 nm, and layer 5 at 100.0 nm yielded the peak score of 0.95315. When bounds were relaxed in subsequent rounds, layer 6 contracted to 90.4499 nm (candidate 2) and 94.7129 nm (candidate 4), perfectly tracking the score collapse to 0.83913 and 0.83504. Constraining the next run to the vicinity of the verified 131.0 nm path length anchors the search in the actual resonance window that produced the highest measured objective value.
